Its LOGIC branch (self-contained state-machine demo) is the usable half here; the UI branch is inapplicable and simply goes unused.

target: 7 lines across 6 skills (tdd:38, implement:13, to-spec:9, to-tickets:11+60, triage:43, wayfinder:25)
reason: Upstream references to skills we do not vendor. Necessity: a dangling skill name misroutes; implement:13's /code-review is worse than dangling because it RESOLVES on machines with the official review plugin enabled, silently answering from a git-diff reviewer on a P4 changelist. Enumerated by grep, not by hand -- three review rounds of hand-enumeration each missed lines. Guarded by the CONTRIBUTING release-checklist grep and by vendored-hashes.json's declared-divergence list.

Upstream uses `claimed` only as wayfinder CONCURRENCY vocabulary (issue-tracker-local.md 'Wayfinding operations'), not as a general lifecycle state. We extend it to the implementation lane, replacing our old work-in-progress. Divergence-by-extension, deliberate: it keeps one vocabulary across both kinds of effort. Disambiguation is by effort, not ticket -- a wayfinder effort has map.md, an implementation effort has spec.md.

NOT a divergence on inspection, recorded so it is not re-litigated: upstream's triage-labels.md is explicitly a per-repo MAPPING TABLE ('Edit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use') and its five names are triage ROLES, not a repo's whole Status vocabulary. Upstream's own local-tracker spec USES `resolved` (wayfinder writes it). Dropping it would have been a divergence FROM upstream, and would have stranded 47 live tickets, 44 of which carry no Outstanding: line to fall back on.
